body:
Hi, @radcortez, have you tried specifying reflection config for Graal? I had just the same issue and it worked for me. Basically, it takes a .json file which contains metadata on all classes that utilize reflection (and ServletConfigEtc certainly does) in your project. This .json is then fed to the GraalVM so that it could instantiate classes on build-time with reflective access preserved.

It is documented on Quarkus page [here](https://quarkus.io/guides/writing-native-applications-tips). To assemble such a file you can use built-in GVM tool called 'native-agent', which is available from your GMV distribution (see [here](https://github.com/oracle/graal/blob/master/substratevm/RESOURCES.md) and [also here](https://github.com/oracle/graal/blob/master/substratevm/CONFIGURE.md) for more information on how to configure it. The agent will produce this file for you, but it takes some use-case coverage, because GraalVM agent will only pick metadata that were accessed in runtime.

As a result you will get a relatively big .json (~60kbs for my project), which you can definetely sift through, since Graal is oblivious on which classes are already configured for reflection on the Quarkus side. Takes some time to do it though :) Hope it helps.

BTW, @geoand I'm not sure who to address this point to (I just saw you in discussion frequently :) ), but I think it would make sense to add reference to [this](https://github.com/oracle/graal/blob/master/substratevm/CONFIGURE.md) to the Quarkus page too.

> BTW, @geoand I'm not sure who to address this point to (I just saw you in discussion frequently :) ), but I think it would make sense to add reference to [this](https://github.com/oracle/graal/blob/master/substratevm/CONFIGURE.md) to the Quarkus page too.

That process should rarely be needed, unless your **application** code does a ton of reflection on its own.
Perhaps we can add a reference to it somewhere in https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/d5e643d5bfabde67ce1cfd143e5bd2f5861d198d/docs/src/main/asciidoc/writing-native-applications-tips.adoc

@geoand, actually, my problem was pretty close to what is described in this issue: Graal threw this
```
Error: Classes that should be initialized at run time got initialized during image building:
org.jboss.resteasy.microprofile.config.ServletConfigSourceImpl
```
, which is quite nasty, because it originated from what Quarkus delivered. It may have caused some odd error case with my project, but the failure description was very confusing. I guess in no-idea-what-to-do-next cases native agent might be quite useful.
Yes, the case here is that adding your own reflection metadata shouldn't be needed.
This issue can easily be fixed in isolation but I am looking into whether there is a more general issue with the opentracing extension

This problem is caused by `org.jboss.resteasy.microprofile.config.ServletConfigSource` being on the classpath but not being registered for reflection.

That is easy enough to solve, but I think that the opentracing extension has a more serious issue, see https://quarkusio.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/187038-dev

issue.title: RestEasy ServletConfigSourceImpl is broken
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
`org.jboss.resteasy.microprofile.config.ServletConfigSourceImpl` is essentially nonfunctional in a native image.  In addition it is context-sensitive which can lead to unexpected behaviors (specifically that two reads of the same key from the same configuration object will yield the same value).

For now I've blacklisted this implementation from being registered to the native image, but it really needs to be revamped or removed.

If we want to support context-sensitive configuration then we need to add that support to Quarkus in such a way that each context gets its own `Config` instance.
